BiblicalUsage: A farmer works land he may not own, and the prophets use his labour as the picture of a people's life. In Amos 5:16 the husbandman is called to mourning, in Isaiah 61:5 strangers shall stand and feed your flocks, and the sons of the alien shall be your plowmen, in Jeremiah 14:4 the ground is chapt because there is no rain, and the plowmen are ashamed, and in Joel 1:11 the husbandmen howl because the harvest of the field is perished.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that the farmer's grief in these verses is the grief of a people who forgot the Lord of the harvest. When the rain stops, the field tells the truth about the nation.
